newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korea's Kia Motors 1996 profit falls.
newsitem.headline: S.Korea's Kia Motors 1996 profit falls.

text.p: Kia Motors Corp, South Korea's second largest carmaker, said on Thursday an economic downturn at home combined with a depreciating yen hit profitability hard in 1996.
Analysts said the company's sales were also affected by its failure to launch major new models during the year.
"An economic downturn is largely to blame for the fall. Competition on the domestic market was severe," said Kwon Yong-joon, a Kia spokesman.
Kia said its profit for calendar 1996 dropped 38.7 percent to 7.04 billion won ($8.17 million) from 11.48 billion won in 1995.
Brisk exports helped push overall sales higher to 6.61 trillion won in 1996 from 5.69 trillion won.
However, the 1996 sales were far below the company's target of 7.4 trillion won, Kia said.
"Labour unrest in June cost about 300 billion won in lost production," said Koo Tae-kyong, an analyst at Kia's planning division.
He said a total of 770,147 vehicles were sold in 1996, up from 712,672.
Domestic sales rose slightly to 447,213 units in 1996 from 441,833 in 1995 as purchases of durable goods such as cars slowed in line with the weakening economy.

Analysts said the yen's depreciation against the dollar made Japanese cars more competitive against Korean products abroad, and at the same time the domestic market was near saturation with little demand from first-time car buyers.
Exports grew at a slower than expected pace, rising to 322,934 units from 270,839, Kia said.
"Exports fell short of meeting our targets because of the low yen," Koo said. He did not say how much the company had hoped to sell overseas.
"Kia's sales were also weak because it had no major new models in 1996, while rivals were actively introducing them," said an analyst at Daishin Economic Research Institute.
The debut of Hyundai Motor's Tiburon compact sedan and Daewoo Motor's Lanos model hit sales of Kia's Avella and Sephia compact cars. Hyundai is South Korea's largest car maker.
Kia said Avella sales on the domestic market dropped to 33,807 units in 1996 from 43,319 in 1995, while Sephia sales fell to 94,490 units from 110,778.
Sales of Credos sedans, Kia's flagship model, were also sluggish, hit by the popularity of Hyundai's Sonata III.
"We aimed to sell more than 10,000 Credos a month. But actual sales were only 8,500 because of Hyundai's Sonata III," Koo said.
Kia has set its sales target at 8.4 trillion won, or 950,000 vehicles, for this year. It hopes to sell 540,000 units domestically and export 410,000 units.
"We will begin marketing luxury Enterprise sedans in March and an upgrade of Sephia in June. We bank on these models for this year's sales," Koo said.
